sec: Diabetic ketoacidosis: pathophysiology, features and investigations

items.q: Match the DKA pathophysiology step to the next printed step — 1) Absolute insulin deficiency 2) Increased CPT-1 3) Free fatty acids 4) Acetyl-CoA … A) With counter-regulatory hormones B) Lipolysis and beta-oxidation in mitochondria C) Undergo beta-oxidation D) Increased ketone-body formation
items.exp: The flow begins with absolute insulin deficiency and counter-regulatory hormones, increased CPT-1, free-fatty-acid beta-oxidation, acetyl-CoA formation and ketone bodies. (Book p930)

items.q: Free fatty acids undergo ___ in the mitochondria in the DKA flowchart.
items.exp: The DKA diagram states that free fatty acids undergo beta-oxidation in mitochondria. (Book p930)

items.q: Assess the DKA flow: I Increased acetyl-CoA formation precedes ketone-body formation. II The endpoint shown is ketosis/ketoacidosis.
items.exp: Both arrows are visible in the DKA pathophysiology sequence. (Book p930)

items.q: In the comparison written at the top of the page, absolute insulin deficiency is greater in which direction?
items.exp: The page annotates absolute insulin deficiency as T1DM >> T2DM. (Book p930)

items.q: A child with DKA is being monitored for the page's highlighted complication associated with increased mortality. What is it?
items.exp: The note states that cerebral edema is seen in children and increases mortality. (Book p930)

items.q: Match the DKA clinical item to the printed category — 1) Nausea/vomiting 2) Respiratory distress out of proportion to lung signs 3) Fruity odour 4) High-anion-gap metabolic acidosis … A) Symptom B) Sign C) Acidotic breath sign D) Investigation finding
items.exp: The page places nausea/vomiting under symptoms, respiratory distress under signs, fruity odour under acidotic breath, and HAGMA under investigations. (Book p930)

items.q: Which symptom is listed alongside thirst/polyuria in DKA?
items.exp: The symptoms list includes nausea/vomiting, thirst/polyuria, abdominal pain and shortness of breath. (Book p930)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the DKA signs listed on the page?
items.exp: The signs list dehydration, tachycardia, respiratory distress, acidotic breath and abdominal tenderness; bradycardia is not listed. (Book p930)

items.q: Match the investigation to the exact DKA investigation list — 1) ABG 2) Beta-hydroxybutyrate 3) Urine 4) Blood tests … A) HAGMA B) Level C) Ketones D) CBC, RFT and serum electrolytes
items.exp: The investigation list includes ABG showing HAGMA, beta-hydroxybutyrate level, urine ketones, CBC, RFT and serum electrolytes. (Book p930)

items.q: Abdominal tenderness in this DKA page is noted as requiring a differential diagnosis of:
items.exp: The page annotates abdominal tenderness with differential diagnosis of acute pancreatitis. (Book p930)

items.q: Assess the counter-regulatory-hormone note: I Glucagon, epinephrine and cortisol are named. II Proteolysis increases gluconeogenic substrates.
items.exp: The page names glucagon, epinephrine and cortisol and draws proteolysis leading to increased gluconeogenic substrates. (Book p930)

items.q: The right-hand DKA flow runs from uncontrolled hyperglycemia through osmotic diuresis to ECF volume ___.
items.exp: The page's right-hand flow ends osmotic diuresis followed by ECF volume depletion. (Book p930)
